Number of knowledge (training) organizations (x TVET level education organizations and x practical, farm-level training organizations) in East Africa are effectively utilizing a dairy blended learning programme through the platform. You could also list here the curricula that have been transformed in blended learning approaches.

31-10-2022: The earned is actually not about producing curricula, but content that is to be used in existing curricula. The blended learning enhances the way of delivering the training, we are not to define what they need to learn for their graduation. The blended learning platform is constructed according to the principle of "all you can learn". This is an ongoing development process of ever increasing content and offers a choice of learning modules. The foundation where the platform is maintained is continuing in the future, long time. So for all possible curricula in the dairy training sector there will be learning pathways available. Even possibly we will cross the boundary of dairy to management and even more. But in none of these cases we develop curricula, but immediately usable modules with up to date material.
Besides modifications other full learning modules have been added and will continue to be added in the DDA. At the end of the second project year the final stage of review was reached for a dairy health module and to be released in February 2022. And another module, Young stock rearing, is also in progress. There are some quality issues in this module though, but this is scheduled for improvement in the near future. Soon even there will be a module of entrepreneurship ready for entering the review stage.

31-10-2022: From March 2021, pilots have started in Kenya and a month later also in Uganda. Ethiopia only followed in September 2021 due to delays due to infrastructure problems. For the pilots, the teachers who were trained in the first training of trainers in 2020 have been conducting the pilots. For the implementation of the pilots, smartphones have been given on loan for all students. The goal was to enroll 30 students per institution in the pilot. However, it turned out that this was difficult. Some schools have classes of more than 80 students. The preference of the trainers was to have all students participate in the course. This would mean that all students would also have to be licensed. However, the budget was not sufficient for this, so in these cases only a part of the classes were enrolled in the courses. But it needs to be said: the demand was much higher than the numbers indicating here.

31-10-2022: The aim of this project is not to support SME's directly. SME's are supported by training of educated staff who are able to enhance the production capacity of the dairy farmers, as wel as training of extension workers in the use of Blended Learning for direct support of Farmers by training them in improved Dairy management. title.narrative: A.S.5. Number of improvements in (inter)national policies/laws

comment.narrative: 21-05-2021: This project did not start actually before 1 Jan 2020.
21-05-2021: We have initially engaged national policy makers, but it has not yet resulted in change of national policy. Is scheduled for next year.
3 Policy briefs, one for each country, provide lessons learned and promote blended learning at TVET level (shared within stakeholder workshop).

31-10-2022: In Kenya and Uganda there is a change in policy of the ministry of education. In both countries the representatives of the ministry of educations have stated in National exchange workshops that for them they see Blended Learning as the way forward. This has provided the TVETS a boost in sustainability of using Blended Learning, because they are now allowed to use tuition fees for licenses for the DDA platform. Licenses have now reduced to 12-20 Euros per student because of the large amount of subscriptions. Brainstud, the platform where the Blended learning is launched from, has made institutional licenses possible. If the numbers of students are high, then the cost per student will be very low. All related TVETS have said this price to be very reasonable, and therefore the decision to adopt this is whether they really want this or not. In Ethiopia there is a similar process going on, but the policy is different. FTVETI, out country A partner plays an important role in the change of policy.

The Earned project is a cue for a number on institutes to formalize their agreements because the importance of including the sector in education is growing due to the introduction of blended learning. Ugandan and Ethiopian TVET's were obviously more aware of formalizing some of the agreements they have. | 31-10-2022: What we count here is all formal partnerships within the dairy sector which are of positive influence to the dairy training and education.
